messages:
Alice Morgan: Quick sanity check — I'm drafting a short experiment plan to compare replayed traffic vs synthetic load for the kernel-selection and batching changes next week. High level and a few concrete measurement items below, please skim and comment.

Ben Tao: :eyes: looks good. A couple quick Qs: how are you defining TTFT vs TPOT here?

Alice Morgan: Good call, I'll be explicit. Proposed metric defs —
```
TTFT = time from request arrival at ingress to first token emitted by the runtime (ms)
TPOT = per-output-token latency distribution (ms/token), measured from kernel entry to token emission; report median/mean/p95/p99
Goodput = tokens generated by the runtime per second, excluding tokens served from prefix/KV cache hits
QPS = number of requests accepted per second (includes cached-hit requests)
```
Also: record token counts including cached-vs-noncached, and label traces with kernel name (fused-attn, matmul-ep, int8-kernel-v2, etc.).

Carlos Rivera: Add sequence-length buckets (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) and a cold/warm KV-cache phase. For replay harness we need prefix distributions and realistic user start times — otherwise synthetic step-load will bias batching behavior.

Alice Morgan: Agreed. Plan outline:
- Phase A: Cold start replay (KV cache empty) using 24h capture sample, preserve arrival times (replay speed control x1 and x4).
- Phase B: Warmed replay (preload KV keys from same capture, then replay) to measure steady-state goodput and kernel mix.
- Phase C: Synthetic profiles: (i) step increase QPS, (ii) bursty Poisson p=0.7 with same seq-len distribution, (iii) uniform small prompts to stress batching.
- For each phase run: baseline kernel selection, candidate kernel set, and per-kernel A/B routing.

Dana Schultz: How do we do apples-to-apples comparing kernel variants? We should pin everything else (same model weights, same quantization profile, same batch timeout and max-batch). Also collect GPU SM utilization and kernel-level occupancy. If TTFT improves but goodput drops, that's a regression for throughput-sensitive SLAs.

Ben Tao: Also surface the tail breakdown by kernel: e.g. p99 TTFT where kernel==int8-kernel-v2 vs kernel==fused-attn. That helps identify whether a single slow kernel is killing tails.

Alice Morgan: Agreed. Implementation notes:
- Add trace tag "experiment_id" and "kernel_choice" to runtime spans.
- Export a CSV per run with columns: run_id, phase, qps_target, seq_bucket, cache_hit_rate, TTFT_p50,p95,p99, TPOT_p50,p95,p99, goodput.
- Use playback harness flag --preserve-arrivals to keep batching behavior.

Carlos Rivera: Quick example of the replay command we'll use: 
```
./replay_harness --input capture_2026-02-10.json --preserve-arrivals --warmup-keys=1e6 --rate=1.0 --tag=exp42-phaseA
```
Replace --rate=4.0 for the x4 run.

Dana Schultz: Regression gating thresholds proposal:
- TTFT_p95 increase > 15% => FAIL
- goodput drop > 10% => FAIL
- any p99 TPOT increase > 20% => FAIL
We should post a summary to perf channel automatically and open a CI ticket if FAIL.

Ben Tao: We should also compute "effective tokens/sec per GPU" (goodput / #gpus) and show allocation efficiency.

perf-bot: [automated note] I'll run the baseline vs candidate comparison once you upload the CSVs to /perf/runs/exp42/. Use tag exp42 in traces for auto-correlation.

Alice Morgan: Nice. Last ask: folks, flag any missing signals. I'm going to spin up Phase A tomorrow and attach initial CSVs. Thanks! :+1:

Carlos Rivera: One more: capture the fraction of requests that hit cached prefixes but still go through the runtime (to measure routing overhead).
